title: In Her Second Cry of Independence, Sheinbaum Reasserted National Sovereignty
author: Contralínea
content:
_This article originally appeared in the[September 16, 2026 edition of
Contralinea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/en-su-segundo-grito-de-
independencia-sheinbaum-reivindico-soberania-nacional/), one of Mexico's
leading investigative journalism outlets._

**Mexico City**. From the presidential balcony of the National Palace, and
before a Mexico City Zocalo packed with people, President Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo delivered her second Cry of Independence, commemorating the 216th
anniversary of the heroic feat. As it closed, she **reasserted national
sovereignty** : "Long live a free, independent, and sovereign Mexico!" "Long
live!" rang out in unison among those in attendance, amid a jubilation that
spread across the historic center of Mexico City.

![An honor guard presents the national flag inside the National
Palace](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-16-second-cry-sovereignty-flag.jpg)Photo:
Jessica Ramirez/Presidencia

She reiterated this stance this morning, during the military parade.
"September 16, Independence Day, is the living memory of Mexico. It always
means holding our heads high and shouting to the four winds that: **Mexico
will never be anyone 's colony or protectorate!** Long live Independence! Long
live sovereignty! May Mexico live forever, long live Mexico, long live
Mexico!"

> Mexico does not bow down, does not kneel, and Mexico is never for sale.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

![President Sheinbaum reviews the troops during the Independence military
parade](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-16-second-cry-sovereignty-parade.jpg)Photo:
Cuartoscuro

Before the troops of the Army, the Navy, and the National Guard who marched,
as well as the people who gathered to witness it, Sheinbaum Pardo stated that
"it is the responsibility of all generations of Mexican women and men to honor
what cost lives: to defend the homeland, safeguard sovereignty, and make
social justice a reality, for which so many have given their lives."

She added that, even though some people might wish otherwise, "Mexico cannot
be understood without its noble, brave, and hardworking people. Nor can it be
understood without its constant struggle for sovereignty and independence.
Because in the early morning of September 16, 1810, something was born that
has accompanied our people for more than two centuries: **the conviction that
freedom is won, sovereignty is defended, and a just and dignified homeland is
built every day**."

Beyond recalling history, the president also noted that it is that heroic feat
of the people, of the heroes and heroines, that "motivates us today. It is the
example of our people who have always fought to decide their own destiny; it
is the pride of a people who knew how to stand with Hidalgo and Morelos; it is
the pride of those who take their destiny into their own hands."

Below is the second Cry of Independence that the President of the Republic,
Dr. Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, delivered on the night of September 15 from the
National Palace, before ringing the bell:

![President Sheinbaum wearing the presidential
sash](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-16-second-cry-sovereignty-portrait.jpg)Photo:
Hazel Cardenas/Presidencia

Mexican women, Mexican men:

  * Long live Independence!
  * Long live Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla!
  * Long live Josefa Ortiz Tellez-Giron!
  * Long live Jose Maria Morelos y Pavon!
  * Long live Leona Vicario!
  * Long live Vicente Guerrero!
  * Long live Gertrudis Bocanegra!
  * Long live Guadalupe Victoria!
  * Long live Antonia Nava!
  * Long live the heroines and heroes who gave us a homeland!
  * Long live the Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples!
  * Long live our migrant sisters and brothers!
  * Long live the dignity of the people of Mexico!
  * Long live freedom!
  * Long live equality!
  * Long live justice!
  * Long live democracy!
  * Long live a free, independent, and sovereign Mexico!
  * Long live Mexico!
  * Long live Mexico!
  * Long live Mexico!

![Aerial view of the packed Zócalo during the Cry of
Independence](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-16-second-cry-sovereignty-aerial.jpg)Photo:
Jose Luis Conde/Presidencia
